tagline: Three thousand feet down from the pass to the basin.
intro: Route 120 leaves Yosemite at Tioga Pass, 9,945 feet up. The approach from the west is gradual. On the east side the road drops more than 3,000 feet in about 12 miles, down Lee Vining Canyon to Mono Lake.

Lee Vining Creek keeps it company, falling from Ellery Lake into the canyon on its way to the lake. Cutting the road along the sheer canyon walls in the 1930s gave its builders more trouble than any other part of the crossing.

moments.title: Tioga Pass
moments.text: Stone buildings with heavy log roofs, built in 1931 and 1934, mark Yosemite's eastern entrance at the crest of the highway.

moments.title: Tioga Lake
moments.text: A glacial lake lies alongside Route 120 near the pass, where frost remains possible even in July.

moments.title: Lee Vining
moments.text: At the foot of the canyon, the town once also called Poverty Flat keeps the Upside-Down House, built by silent-film actress Nellie Bly O'Bryan.

practical: Tioga Pass closes in winter because of snow; opening and closing dates vary considerably.
